newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end off sharply, beef turns lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end off sharply, beef turns lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed sharply down as cash beef prices reversed direction after their recent run-up.

Floor sources noted concern had been growing that boxes of beef were stacking up as packers struggled to move supplies following the rise in prices. Movement only picked up slightly Tuesday when packers started to sell at lower prices.
USDA said boxed beef cut-out values Tuesday were off $0.88 to $1.96 per cwt with 248 fabricated loads traded.
Slow beef sales quashed sentiment that higher prices would be paid for cash cattle this week.
After the close trade developed at $65 per cwt, down $1 from the bulk of trade last week. Earlier in the week many had been looking for cash cattle to trade up $1 at $67.
Floor sources said R.J. O'Brien was a featured seller of both August and October live cattle on the day. Lind Waldock were a featured seller of August and Refco of October.
Noted buyers included E.D. and F. Man International (August), Cargill Investor Services (August and October late), LIT and locals, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures also closed lower, weakened partly by spillover selling from the live cattle pit.
Dealers said, however, there was growing concern that feeder cattle futures' five-month uptrend may have run its course and the market may be overpriced.
"You can buy feeders put them on feed and lose $50 a head. Feeders are too high," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities.
Sharp losses in CBOT corn helped to limit losses.
The latest CME feeder cattle index, for August 4, was down $0.25 at $82.31 per cwt.
Boneless beef futures were lower, weakened by commercial selling.
Floor sources noted Cargill Investor Services was an active seller of August boneless beef which closed off 1.10 cent at 100.40 cents a lb.
Beef trimmings futures were also lower with August off 0.50 cent at 45.50 cents a lb.
